LanguageData.CC_SetNote_NewPeoples: Now and then a new people comes into being from what happened in the region, with a town of its own a few days off.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_NewPeoples_Tip: How often a new people arises from what happened in the region: the survivors of a town that fell in a fight settle together (two fallen towns in five), merchants or herders of three prospering towns of two peoples or more band together as a league, one the council sent away gathers a band and leads it (half of them), and with Ideology faithful break away after a war of words over their faith (half the time). Each takes the ways of one of Rimfolk's peoples by its age and its place: survivors may take to the river as river folk where one runs near, a band led by a learned one may keep a school as scholars, a league of spacer-age towns trades as an enclave, and faithful who broke away may walk the roads as pilgrims. Each has a name and an emblem colour of its own; a town a few days from what made it; and goodwill by what happened, never an enemy or an ally on its first day. A letter tells it. At 100% (the default) one arises every 40 days at most and one of the same cause every 90, none before the world's 15th day, and six at most stand at once. 200% halves the waits; 0% switches it off.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_refugees: {MEANS}: the survivors of {TOWN}, the town of {PEOPLE} that fell {AGO}, did not scatter. They have stayed together, and they go by a name of their own now: {NAME}.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_refugees_2: {MEANS}: those who lived through the fall of {TOWN} {AGO} have kept together, people of {PEOPLE} with nothing left to go back to. They go by a name of their own now: {NAME}.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_refugees_Last: {PEOPLE} have no other town, and these are the last of them.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_refugees_herders: They saved what beasts they could, and they keep to the open grass with them rather than build walls again.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_refugees_herders_2: They saved what beasts they could, and they keep to the open grass with them, counting every head at dusk, as the herders do.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_refugees_healers: They began by tending their own wounded, and they keep a sickhouse now for anyone who comes to its door.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_refugees_healers_2: They began by tending their own wounded, and they keep a sickhouse now, with lamps lit at its gate for anyone on the road at night.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_refugees_traders: With their fields lost, they carry goods between the towns, and they keep a waystation on the road.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_refugees_traders_2: With their fields lost, they carry goods between the towns from a waystation on the road, and they mean to be written in good ink by every town they deal with.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_refugees_fishers: They took to the river near the ruin, and they live by its fish and its ferry now, from a landing on the bank.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_refugees_fishers_2: They took to the river near the ruin, and they live by its fish and its ferry now, from a landing on the bank, pulling whoever is in the water out first.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_refugees_sextons: They stayed to bury the town's dead, every one, friend and foe, and they keep a grave-garden by the ruin now with a bell, for the dead of anyone who will bring them.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_refugees_sextons_2: They buried the town's dead one by one and rang once over every grave, as the Quiet Bell does, and they keep a grave-garden by the ruin now for everyone's.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_refugees_salvagers: They put what was left of the town on wheels and runners and drove it out of the ruin, and they have not stopped since: a yard on the move, buying what others throw away.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_refugees_salvagers_2: They loaded what the fire left onto carts and rolled away from the ruin, a brass cog stitched to every shoulder, and nobody among them has voted to stop.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_refugees_Cool: They are wary of the colony, as their old people were.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_refugees_CoolOurs: They remember who burned {TOWN}, and they are cool toward the colony.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_refugees_Warm: They have heard the colony was a friend to {PEOPLE}, and they would be glad of its friendship too.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_refugees_Plain: They have no quarrel with the colony.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_league_Title: {NAME}: a league of the region's towns
LanguageData.CC_Arise_league_traders: {MEANS}: the merchants of {TOWNS} have banded together as one league, {NAME}, to keep the roads between their towns open and their caravans guarded.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_league_herders: {MEANS}: herders from the camps of {TOWNS} have joined their herds and their grazing as one folk, {NAME}.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_league_brokers: {MEANS}: the merchants of {TOWNS} have banded together as an enclave of brokers, {NAME}, trading between the towns below and the ships above from a market round a landing pad.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_league_brokers_2: {MEANS}: the merchants of {TOWNS} have banded together as an enclave of brokers, {NAME}, who keep every bargain to the last digit and trade between the towns below and the ships above from a market round a landing pad.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_league_Cool: Their towns have no love for the colony, and neither have they.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_league_Warm: They know the colony's name from their towns, and they would be glad to see its traders.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_league_Plain: They have yet to make up their minds about the colony.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_exiles: {MEANS}: {PAWN_nameDef}, {WORD} by the council {AGO}, did not go far. Others with nowhere to go have gathered round {PAWN_objective}, and they go by a name of their own now: {NAME}, with {PAWN_nameDef} at their head.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_exiles_herders: They keep a few beasts on the grazing there, and they take in whoever else has been turned out.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_exiles_traders: They hire out on the roads as carriers and guards, and they keep a waystation of their own.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_exiles_fishers: They keep boats on the river there, fishing and ferrying from a landing of their own, and take in whoever else has been turned out.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_exiles_scholars: {PAWN_nameDef} has them reading and copying, and they keep an archive of their own, open to anyone who can read.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_exiles_scholars_2: {PAWN_nameDef} has them copying whatever they can find before it is lost, and they keep an archive of their own, open to anyone who can read.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_exiles_tamers: {PAWN_nameDef} has a way with beasts, and they walk the region with companions of their own now, challenging every keeper of beasts they meet to a friendly bout.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_exiles_tamers_2: {PAWN_nameDef} taught them that a bond is not a leash, and they keep bout-rings and stables now, a token on their sashes for every bout won fairly.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_exiles_hunters: {PAWN_nameDef} is a fine shot, and they follow the region's great beasts now, lighting a lantern at every crossroads where one took someone.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_exiles_hunters_2: {PAWN_nameDef} taught them to track and to keep a book of every beast run down, and they keep lanterns lit at the crossroads until each page has its ending.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_exiles_Cool: Those who have met {PAWN_nameDef} on the road say {PAWN_pronoun} has not forgiven the colony.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_exiles_CoolGlad: {PAWN_nameDef} has not forgotten who was glad to see {PAWN_objective} go, they say.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_exiles_Warm: {PAWN_nameDef} bears the colony no grudge, they say.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_exiles_WarmFriend: {PAWN_nameDef} asks after {FRIEND}, they say, and bears the colony no grudge.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_exiles_Plain: {PAWN_nameDef} wishes the colony neither well nor ill, they say.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_splinter: {MEANS}: the war of words between the preachers of {PEOPLE} and their neighbours has cooled, but not all of {PEOPLE}'s faithful came back from it. Those who broke away have gone off together as {NAME}, and their creed has a name of its own now: {NEWFAITH}.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_splinter_StandIn: {MEANS}: not all of {PEOPLE}'s faithful hold with their preachers. Those who broke away have gone off together as {NAME}, and their creed has a name of its own now: {NEWFAITH}.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_splinter_dropped: They keep {FAITH} but for its {MEME} teaching.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_splinter_added: They keep {FAITH}, and they hold to a {MEME} teaching besides.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_splinter_healers: They have taken vows, and they keep a sickhouse, as they say the faith first asked of its people.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_splinter_herders: They took their herds with them, and they keep to the open grass, apart from the old camps.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_splinter_pilgrims: They walk the roads between the faith's old shrines, as they say its first believers did, and keep a hostel for those on the road.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_splinter_pilgrims_2: They walk the roads between the faith's old shrines with a shell for every shrine they reach, and keep a hostel for those on the road.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_splinter_Parent: {PEOPLE} call them heretics, and there is no love lost between the two.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_splinter_Warm: They remember the colony's fair table in the debate, and they think well of it.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_splinter_Plain: They have no quarrel with the colony.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_splinter_Cool: They keep their distance from the colony.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_H_refugees: The survivors of {FROM} settled together as {NAME}.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_H_exiles: {FROM}, sent away by the council, gathered a band of their own: {NAME}.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_H_splinter: Faithful of {PEOPLE} broke away from {FROM} as {NAME}.

LanguageData.CC_Arise_Card_exiles: Arose {AGO}: gathered round {FROM}, whom the council sent away.
LanguageData.CC_Arise_Card_splinter: Arose {AGO}: faithful of {PEOPLE} who broke away from {FROM}.
